chapter: Louis Armstrong, King Oliver and St. Louis memories
title: "The mothers" who fed traveling bands
summary: Thomas praises the women who cooked clean, wholesome meals for musicians on the road, including Mom Baker near the Apollo.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: In those days, Stan, there were people they called the mothers. They called themselves, no, they didn't call themselves, I guess we gave them the name of the mothers. And I think that was one of the most important things in the music business. Babe and I Dave Reynolds was talking about that tonight. They prepared the food for you and the food was the best food they could buy, you know. It was clean and it was good food. It was raised, it like you say you raised maybe whatever the thing was, maybe a nickel and they explained to me why it was raised (?). Now the only hassle came when some damn fool came to join the band who never traveled before and say, "Well, lookee here. You know what happened?" Now if you were talking to me then I could shush him because always a time when the waitress was there, the mother was there. This is real cheap so the time you came brothers ... back, not with the mothers, / the food was raised 10 cents or 25 cents.
When you call them the mothers, who were they?

Well, I gotta remember. I gotta tell you this. Mom Charleston, Philadelphia and she saved Philadelphia for me because I thought that was possibly the worst town on earth. It's not too much better now. And, Atlanta, what's that lady's name in Atlanta. I'll get to it pretty soon. And, New York, it was Mom Baker right across from the Apollo, backstage.
Oh, these ladies really looked after theatrical people.

And they meant it and they cooked wholesome food and you never had a piece of bread. We had biscuits. We had rolls, you know. And I think they were very important. A lot of people have forgotten about them but they were important to me.
Yeah. They must have been every important to musicians.
Yeah, and I tell you the food was clean. There was no grease. All fresh food.
